facts.content: Patient reports intermittent frontal headaches at work as the chief complaint.
facts.source_text: CC: Intermittent frontal headaches at work

facts.content: Patient reports that headaches have increased since a job change.
Headaches occur during computer or meeting work.
Headaches are associated with mild nausea.
Patient reports no prior history of headaches.
Patient reports episodic tingling and prickling in both hands.
Patient reports palpitations about once per day.
Patient reports episodic shortness of breath while seated.
Patient reports no shortness of breath with exercise.
Patient reports decreased appetite.
Patient reports unintentional 5 pound weight loss.
Patient notes that clothes size is unchanged despite weight loss.
Patient reports decreased libido since job change.
Patient rates work stress as 7 to 8 out of 10.
Patient has a history of hypothyroidism.
Patient is taking thyroxine, with dose and route not known.
Patient denies any allergies.
Patient works as a lawyer in London.
Patient drinks approximately two glasses of alcohol weekly.
Patient does not smoke.
Patient does not use recreational drugs.
No vital signs or physical examination findings are documented.
